name: Paumarí
catalog_quote: (1) Secondary stress is placed on every odd-numbered mora from right-to-left. (2) Primary stress is placed on the antepenultimate mora; in words of less than three moras in length it is placed on the final (rightmost) mora.
sweep_summary: Only one works with stress in the title (Everett 2003, already listed); it is squarely about Paumari word stress and was downloaded open from the journal of record (Linguistic Discovery, DOI resolves 200 to journals.dartmouth.edu; PDF document/512 saved) and read: p. 23 states primary stress on the antepenultimate mora with alternating right-to-left secondary stress, final stress in sub-trimoraic words -- verbatim identical to the catalog's deciding quotation, so the fixed-strict antepenultimate coding is confirmed, not superseded. Cross-checked against the held SIL Chapman & Odmark 1964/2009 phonemic statement (p. 7: antepenult; no final stress; disyllables initial), which agrees for 3+ syllables and differs only on disyllables (a point the rule string is neutral on) and flags reduplicant-stress variation (also Everett sec. 3.6 / Chapman & Derbyshire 1991:349). No new open source surfaced: archive.org has no Handbook of Amazonian Languages vol. 3 or Rosetta 'pad' items, HathiTrust ISBN lookups are empty, De Gruyter's HAL 3 page (DOI 10.1515/9783110854374) is a bot-challenge/paywall; 348-349).

new_statements.reading: Fixed antepenultimate primary stress in words of three or more moras/syllables (bóvirì, kajóvirì, ìtarápahà), with alternating secondary stress rightward-counted; sub-minimal (two-mora) words take final stress. This is the same passage the catalog already quotes; this search of works with stress in the title re-downloaded it from the journal of record (previously held only as the author-site copy) and confirms the fixed-strict antepenultimate coding. Independent cross-check read this search of works with stress in the title: Chapman & Odmark 1964/2009 'Paumari phonemic statement' (SIL Brasil), sec. VI.C p. 7: 'Stress normally occurs on the ante-penult syllable or on the initial syllable of two syllable words. Stress occurring elsewhere is marked with '.' and p. 7 'Stress does not occur on the final syllable on the word level.' (saved) -- agrees on the antepenult for 3+ syllable words; differs only on disyllables (Chapman initial vs Everett final), which the catalog rule string does not encode.

audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-strict, antepenultimate: antepenultimate stress) rests on Everett 2003, a dedicated open-access stress article; the deciding sentence is verbatim at p.23 sec. 2.2 and the supporting p.25 forms are present. sources.note: Dedicated 23-page first-hand stress study (fieldwork with Paumari speakers; Chapman consulted). Primary stress on the antepenultimate mora (=antepenultimate syllable, CVV syllables counted as monomoraic), secondary stress on every odd-numbered mora counting right-to-left; disyllables and CVV monosyllables are stressed on the final mora (bimoraic minimal word). Analysed as quantity-insensitive right-to-left iambs with antepenultimate primary stress ('the only iambic stress system reported on with antepenultimate stress', p. 39).
